issues.area: Memory budget / D10 confidential GPU isolation
issues.problem: The arithmetic is internally inconsistent. Steady state sums to ~45-50GB (verified). But D10/security-spine mandate a DEDICATED vLLM PROCESS per confidential tenant for KV-cache isolation, and the memory_budget itself says 'budget at most ONE extra confidential vLLM process at a time.' A second vLLM process means a SECOND full resident copy of Qwen3-30B-A3B: ALL 30.5B experts must be resident (~16-18GB weights) PLUS its own KV cache/CUDA context (~4-8GB). 50 + 16 + 4 = 70GB, which exceeds the 64GB ceiling by ~6GB minimum. The whole confidential-drafting path — the centerpiece — cannot run concurrently with the public stack as designed. The brief never accounts for the second model's WEIGHTS, only hand-waves 'within headroom.'
issues.fix: Drop per-process model duplication. Achieve confidential KV-cache isolation on ONE shared vLLM generator process via: (a) strict request serialization with KV-cache flush between confidential and non-confidential requests (vLLM does not leak KV across separate requests by default — the 'leakage' risk is prefix-caching/shared-prefix, so simply disable prefix caching for confidential requests, --enable-prefix-caching=False, and the single-process design is safe); or (b) if true process isolation is required, the confidential process must load a SMALLER model (e.g. the Qwen3-14B dense fallback at ~9GB) and the public 30B must be evicted/paused while it runs. Re-state the budget with explicit weights line items for any second process and prove the sum is <=64GB minus OS.

issues.area: Security spine — crypto-shred of searchable derivatives (D7)
issues.problem: D7/security-spine mandate application-layer AES-256-GCM on 'every confidential derivative (vectors, BM25 postings, graph edges)' BEFORE insert. This is mathematically impossible to then SEARCH: AES-GCM ciphertext destroys the distance metric HNSW/IVF need (verified), and encrypted BM25 postings cannot be tokenized/scored. You cannot run pgvector similarity or BM25 ranking over AES-GCM blobs. So either the confidential vectors are encrypted (and unsearchable, making confidential RAG grounding — the centerpiece STAGE 3 — non-functional) or they are searchable (and NOT crypto-shred-protected). The brief lists the only workable mechanism (per-tenant LUKS/dm-crypt volume + delete-and-rebuild) as a secondary 'fallback,' inverting reality. A 30B builder will follow the stated primary and produce a broken or insecure system.
issues.fix: Make per-tenant LUKS/dm-crypt-encrypted volume(s) + drop-and-rebuild the PRIMARY crypto-shred mechanism for ALL searchable confidential derivatives (vectors, BM25, graph). Reserve application-layer AES-GCM ONLY for at-rest non-searchable blobs (CRDT draft snapshots, autosave, version history, eval traces, cache values) where it works. Crypto-shred for searchable indexes = destroy the per-tenant DEK that unlocks that tenant's LUKS volume / drop the tenant's encrypted tablespace. Rewrite D7 and the security-spine crypto control to say this explicitly and remove the false 'ALE on vectors before insert' instruction.

issues.area: Security spine — hardware root of trust (D7)
issues.problem: D7 anchors the box-master key in 'the Orin OP-TEE/EKB hardware root of trust' and claims 'the Orin already ships a hardware-anchored secure-world key... no cloud needed,' framed as turnkey. Verification shows this is NOT turnkey: it requires (1) provisioning Secure Boot and irreversibly BURNING the OEM_K1/K2 fuse (one-shot, bricks-on-error), (2) writing an OP-TEE Trusted Application in C running in the secure world PLUS a Client Application to expose key-derive/seal to Linux userspace, and (3) NVIDIA's own developer forums show active, unresolved failures ('AES crypto failed: -17', 'EKB extraction failure', 'SSK derivation failure under secure boot'). This is firmware/secure-world C engineering far beyond a Python-writing 30B builder, and is a likely hard build wall that blocks Phase P0.4.
issues.fix: Demote the OP-TEE/EKB hardware anchor to an OPTIONAL hardening step documented for a human operator, NOT a Phase-0 builder deliverable. Make the Phase-0 default the fTPM-via-tpm2-tools path (seal the box-master key to a PCR using the userspace TPM2 stack, which needs no custom TA) OR a passphrase-derived master key entered at boot (KDF, key never on disk). State plainly that fuse-burning Secure Boot is irreversible and out of scope for the automated build. Keep IKms as the seam so the EKB-backed LocalKms can be added later by a human.

issues.area: AI plane — 'vLLM is ONE serving runtime' (D9)
issues.problem: The brief repeatedly claims vLLM 'uniquely serves embeddings AND rerankers in the SAME stack, collapsing three serving systems into one.' Verified: vLLM is strictly ONE model per process; a single `vllm serve` instance cannot host the 30B generator AND bge-m3 embedder AND bge-reranker simultaneously. 'One runtime' actually means THREE separate vLLM processes, each with its own CUDA context (~1-2GB context overhead each, ~3-6GB total) and its own weights — none of which the memory_budget's single 'vLLM KV ~8GB' line accounts for beyond the generator. It also adds operational complexity (3 processes + a router) the brief presents as simplicity.
issues.fix: Correct D9 and the runbook to state 3 vLLM processes (or 1 vLLM for the LLM + sentence-transformers in-process for embed/rerank, which avoids two extra CUDA contexts and may be lighter on Orin). Add the embedder-process and reranker-process CUDA-context + weights to the memory table explicitly. Re-verify the sum. Keep the IModelRouter seam abstracting which process serves what.

issues.area: Embedding stack — bge-m3 AND SPECTER2 both resident
issues.problem: The memory_budget lists ONE embedder (bge-m3 OR Qwen3-Embedding, ~1.5GB). But the retrieval_design and domain model REQUIRE SPECTER2 as a SECOND, concurrently-loaded citation-aware embedding space powering ExpertiseFingerprint and collaborator discovery (the team-assembly axis of the centerpiece). That is a second ~440M model + its own serving path. Additionally SPECTER2 is an ADAPTER on SciBERT requiring the `adapters`/adapter-transformers library and the proximity adapter loaded on the base — extra moving parts the builder must wire, and it cannot be served by vLLM pooling as a simple sentence-transformers model without care.
issues.fix: Add SPECTER2's footprint (~0.5-1GB + adapter library) as a distinct line in the memory budget and a distinct serving entry. Specify it runs via sentence-transformers + adapters on the SM 8.7 PyTorch wheel (not vLLM). Decide and document whether SPECTER2 embeddings are precomputed at ingest (batch, then the model can be UNLOADED at serve time — recommended, saves RAM) vs kept hot. Precompute-at-ingest is the right call for the box; state it.

issues.problem: D8/tech_stack assert VectorChord-BM25 is 'production-grade, claimed 3x faster than Elasticsearch' as justification for collapsing the lexical engine into Postgres. Verification of the project docs shows the fast-scan/BM25 kernel is x86_64-optimized and 'performance may be lower' on aarch64. The 3x-vs-ES benchmark is x86 and does not transfer to Orin. The brief also marks VectorChord IVF+RaBitQ as 'needs-verification' for aarch64 build but still leans on it as the disk-friendly index that makes the >RAM-index story work — that story is unproven on the target.
issues.fix: Make pgvector HNSW + a pure-Postgres/pg_search BM25 the VERIFIED P0 default (already the fallback) and stop citing the x86 3x-ES number as a single-box rationale. Explicitly de-risk: the index MUST fit in RAM/NVMe (the brief already says this), so the 'disk-friendly RaBitQ on a >RAM index' upgrade path is not load-bearing for P0 and should be moved entirely to a P1 'verify-then-adopt' task. Add a P0.5 acceptance test that benchmarks BM25 latency on actual aarch64, not an inherited x86 claim.

issues.area: Corpus freshness factual error (D14, open_risks, memory_budget)
issues.problem: The brief repeatedly 'fixes the stale monthly assumption' by asserting the free OpenAlex snapshot cadence is now QUARTERLY. Verified: OpenAlex still releases a new full snapshot MONTHLY (~330GB gz / ~1.6TB uncompressed). The brief introduces a factual regression while claiming to correct one, and bakes 'quarterly' into the ingestion schedule, the risk register, and the doc set — so the builder will under-schedule refreshes.
issues.fix: Revert to MONTHLY OpenAlex cadence throughout (D14, open_risks, 09-ingestion doc). The ingestion DAG should support monthly delta ingestion partitioned by updated_date (OpenAlex partitions snapshots by updated_date, enabling incremental loads — note this so the builder does delta, not full re-ingest each month).

issues.area: Build phase ordering — P0.4 depends on un-built data plane; P0.6/AI plane needed earlier
issues.problem: Two ordering breaks: (1) P0.4 (confidential KEK stores + crypto-shred for vectors/BM25/graph) is scheduled BEFORE P0.5 (the data plane that creates those vector/BM25/graph stores). You cannot build/test crypto-shred of derivative stores that do not exist yet; the P0.4 acceptance test 'post-crypto-shred zero-decryptable-hits across ALL derivative stores' references sinks built in P0.5. (2) P0.3 classification gate and P0.5 retrieval both need embeddings, but the AI plane (P0.6) that serves the embedder comes AFTER — the earlier phases' acceptance tests implicitly need a running embedder/reranker.
issues.fix: Reorder: bring the AI-plane bring-up (at least the embedder + reranker serving, a slice of P0.6) BEFORE P0.5 so retrieval has embeddings, and BEFORE P0.4 so there are real derivatives to encrypt. Split P0.4 into P0.4a (KEK/DEK + LocalKms + CRDT-snapshot blob encryption — has no store dependency) and P0.4b (per-tenant encrypted tablespace/LUKS crypto-shred of the search indexes) which must run AFTER the data plane P0.5. Make each phase's acceptance tests reference only artifacts built in that phase or earlier.

issues.area: Centerpiece STAGE 3 contradiction — confidential grounding vs public-only index
issues.problem: D6 states confidential content NEVER enters any shared retrieval surface and the expertise graph / discovery are 'public-tier only by construction.' But the collaboration-loop STAGE 3 requires mod-lit-intelligence to ground the confidential proposal draft in 'the shared corpus + PRIOR WINNING PROPOSALS.' Prior winning proposals are confidential-tier per-tenant artifacts. If they can never be indexed (D6), they cannot be retrieved for grounding — yet grounding in them is sold as the moat ('none ground in a shared scholarly corpus'). The brief never specifies HOW confidential prior proposals become retrievable for the SAME tenant without violating the classify-gates-index public-only rule.
issues.fix: Define a per-tenant CONFIDENTIAL retrieval surface distinct from the shared public index: a tenant-scoped, RLS-isolated, per-tenant-DEK-on-an-encrypted-tablespace vector+BM25 index that ONLY that tenant's confidential drafting path can query (enforced at the PEP). Clarify that 'never enters any SHARED index' means the cross-tenant public index, not that confidential content is unindexable for its owning tenant. Add this confidential-own-tenant index to the data model, the memory budget, and a P0.9 acceptance test (tenant A grounds on its own prior proposal; tenant B cannot retrieve it).

issues.area: Federation-readiness false promise — KV/process model and crypto don't carry forward
issues.problem: The brief promises cross-box federation is 'a transport addition, not a rewrite' behind clean seams. But two of the single-box decisions are NOT clean seams: (a) crypto-shred-by-volume-LUKS (the real primary, per issue above) is a node-local filesystem mechanism that does NOT compose with cross-node revocation/replication — the future IRevocationAuthority cannot crypto-shred another node's LUKS volume; (b) the in-Python ABAC + Postgres-CTE ReBAC evaluate against LOCAL tables only — federation needs distributed tuple resolution that the recursive-CTE Check() cannot do across boxes. These are presented as drop-in-replaceable but are semantically different.
issues.fix: Be honest in 15-future-federation-interfaces.md: list crypto-shred-locality and local-only authz resolution as KNOWN federation-boundary rewrites, not transport swaps. Keep the Protocol seams but annotate which carry forward cleanly (PublishableProjection.discoverability_scope, IExchangeFeed) vs which are single-box-only semantics (volume crypto-shred, CTE ReBAC). Removing the 'just a transport addition' over-claim prevents the builder/operator from assuming federation-safety that isn't there.

issues.area: Complexity for a 30B builder — Phase 0 scope is very large
issues.problem: P0.0-P0.10 packs 11 phases including a full security kernel (PEP, fixed decision order, FORCE-RLS with 4 bypass lints, hash-chained audit), per-tenant envelope crypto, hardware-anchored KMS, single-Postgres hybrid retrieval + rerank, a classification-routed model router with process isolation, an HDD-aware DuckDB ingestion pipeline with identity resolution, three feature modules, a CRDT websocket co-authoring server with three editorial modes, AND the async write-back loop — each with adversarial CI gates. This is multiple senior-engineer-quarters of work; expecting a mid-size local model to build it correctly end-to-end, with the security invariants right, is optimistic. The risk register acknowledges the model 'will get one wrong = leak' but the mitigation (more CI gates) presumes the model can also write correct adversarial tests.
issues.fix: Define a genuinely minimal walking-skeleton P0 that proves the LOOP end-to-end with the security spine on the SIMPLEST possible substrate (single tenant pair, one editorial mode = real-time only, classification = allow/quarantine binary, crypto-shred = drop-tenant-tablespace, no SPECTER2 second space, HNSW only). Move suggesting-mode, anchored comments, HippoRAG2, identity-resolution probabilistic blocking, and the hardware key anchor to P1. Have a HUMAN author the security-contract CI gates (they are the safety net; do not trust the 30B to write its own tripwires). Sequence so the loop is demonstrable before breadth of features.

issues.area: DuckDB + Postgres + vLLM(x3) RAM contention at INGEST time
issues.problem: The memory budget is computed for STEADY-STATE serving. But P0.7 ingestion runs DuckDB out-of-core (which, despite spill-to-disk, still wants several GB of working RAM for hash joins/sorts) CONCURRENTLY with the resident model weights and Postgres shared_buffers. The brief says 'serialize generation vs heavy embedding batches' but does not serialize ingestion vs serving, and the async write-back job (D12) also runs DuckDB-style enrichment off the outbox potentially during interactive editing. The ~15-19GB 'headroom' is simultaneously claimed for burst, DuckDB spill, AND the second confidential vLLM process — triple-counted.
issues.fix: State a hard rule: bulk ingestion (P0.7) runs in a maintenance window with model serving paused or with shared_buffers temporarily reduced; cap DuckDB memory with SET memory_limit explicitly (e.g. 8GB) and threads to leave room. For the async write-back, cap its DuckDB/embedding memory and gate it behind a semaphore that yields to interactive generation. Replace the triple-counted 'headroom' with three separate, mutually-exclusive budgets (serve-only, ingest-window, writeback-window) and show each fits.

overall_verdict: The design is strategically sound and unusually self-aware (the loop centerpiece, single-box re-basing, fail-closed security spine, and HDD/NVMe tiering are all well-reasoned), but it ships with FOUR critical build-blockers that a 30B model would hit head-on, plus several high-severity inconsistencies. The four criticals: (1) the memory budget does not fit — a second confidential vLLM process needs a full ~16-18GB second copy of the 30B weights, pushing the total to ~70GB > 64GB; (2) crypto-shred via application-layer AES-GCM on vectors/BM25 is mathematically incompatible with searching them (AES ciphertext destroys distance metrics; encrypted postings cannot be scored) — the brief's stated 'fallback' (per-tenant LUKS + rebuild) is actually the ONLY workable primary; (3) the OP-TEE/EKB hardware key anchor is presented as turnkey but requires irreversible fuse-burning + secure-world C code and shows unresolved failures on NVIDIA's own forums — a hard wall for a Python builder; (4) 'vLLM as ONE runtime for LLM+embedder+reranker' is false — vLLM is one-model-per-process, so it's 3 processes with 3 CUDA contexts the budget never counts. High-severity: SPECTER2 is a REQUIRED second embedding space the budget omits; OpenAlex is MONTHLY not the brief's claimed 'quarterly' (a factual regression); P0.4 crypto-shred is ordered before P0.5 builds the stores it shreds; and the centerpiece's confidential-proposal grounding contradicts the public-only-index rule with no per-tenant confidential retrieval surface defined. Fix the four criticals and the four high-severity items BEFORE the 30B build starts; also cut Phase-0 to a true walking skeleton (real-time editing only, drop-tablespace crypto-shred, no hardware anchor, single embedding space) and have a human — not the 30B — author the security-contract CI tripwires. With those changes the design is buildable; as written, the build fails at memory bring-up, at confidential retrieval, and at the KMS phase.
